info.title: deepertones API
info.description: Every JSON response has an envelope, and `status` equals the HTTP status. Success: `{ success: true, status, message, data }`. Error: `{ success: false, status, message, error: { code, details?, requestId } }`. Branch on `success`, then on `error.code`, not on `message`.

adminToken.description: The shared admin secret (ADMIN_API_TOKEN) for /api/v1/admin. A user access token never opens these routes.

goal.description: One of the six goals the app offers.

dayOneAt.description: When the chase's first ready scan was taken. Null for a fresh start, or while the chase has no ready scan.

resumeUntil.description: The last moment the goal can be taken up again and still resume. Null for a fresh start.

items.description: One thing that changes what is safe for the user, or `none`.

choices.description: What applies, one to 20 entries from the five choices. Repeats are collapsed, so the answer has each choice once. `none` cannot be combined with another choice: 400 `INVALID_SAFETY_ANSWER` with `details.field` `choices`.

reactionText.description: The products or ingredients that gave a reaction, up to 300 characters once trimmed (counted as typed). Line breaks and tabs are fine: every run of whitespace is saved as one space. Optional even when `reaction` is ticked; blank counts as left out. Words without `reaction` ticked are 400 `INVALID_SAFETY_ANSWER` with `details.field` `reactionText`.

prescriptionText.description: The prescription cream or tablets, up to 300 characters once trimmed (counted as typed). Line breaks and tabs are fine: every run of whitespace is saved as one space. Optional even when `prescription` is ticked; blank counts as left out. Words without `prescription` ticked are 400 `INVALID_SAFETY_ANSWER` with `details.field` `prescriptionText`.

budgetBand.description: Null when the user gave none.

updatedAt.description: When the country and band were last saved.

country.description: The country the user shops in, as its two-letter code in the catalog's Countries tab. A code that is not there, or is retired, is 400 `UNKNOWN_COUNTRY`.

budgetBand.description: How much the user is happy to spend on a product: `low`, `mid`, `high`. The bands are per country, each in its own money. Leave it out to have no budget band, which also takes back a band saved earlier. Anything else is 400 `UNKNOWN_BUDGET_BAND`.

entries.description: The products the profile uses, most recently scanned first, at most 200.

id.description: The entry's own id, kept when the product is scanned again. Use it to remove the entry.

addedAt.description: When the product first reached the shelf.

lastScannedAt.description: When it was last scanned. The shelf is ordered by this, newest first.

source.description: The scan and item the entry was last read from.

allOf.description: Only on a `product` entry: the same summary a scan item shows.

usedFor.description: How long the product has been used.

description.description: What the user noted, if anything.

concerns.description: Cautions for a product of unknown contents, worked out from the answers each time the item is shown. Not an analysis of any label.

rulesVersion.description: Which version of the caution rules wrote `concerns`.

noLabel.description: Only on a `no-label` entry: what the user said about it, and the cautions that earns.

scanId.description: The typed scan made for the add. Follow it with `GET /api/v1/scans/products/{scanId}` or its `/events`.

itemId.description: Its one item. When the item is `ready` the product is on the shelf.

removed.description: The ids this call took off the shelf, in the order asked for. An id removed before is accepted but not listed.

entryId.description: A removed entry whose product the current verdict says to stop.

taperCode.description: For a verified user, the step-down to ease off it with: the `code` of an entry of `tapers` in `GET /api/v1/me/verdict`, which carries `whatToExpect` and `seeAProfessionalIf`. `null` for a guest, who is served only the locked verdict preview.

line.description: A fixed plain-words warning to show, which stands on its own: for a guest it points at signing up to see the step-down.

stepDownWarnings.description: In the order asked for. Empty when the verdict is pending, out of date or unavailable, or stops none of the removed products.

entryIds.description: The shelf entries to take off, 1 to 50 different ids, from `GET /api/v1/me/shelf`.

reason.description: Why the products left the shelf, for all of them. Leave it out when the user did not say.

productId.description: The product the entry really is, from `GET /api/v1/products/search`. Not the entry's own product.

reason.description: Why the product left the shelf. Leave it out when the user did not say.

locked.description: A guest is given this preview and never the products: sign up to see them.

fit.description: `not-ready` when the goal-fit check has not answered yet: the products it would decide are shown as kept for now, and it is tried again.

groups.description: All eight headings in the order the screen shows them, each with fixed words and its product count (0 where empty; the app hides the zeros). Copy awaiting the owner's sign-off.

total.description: How many skin-care products the verdict holds.

counts.description: How many products are under each heading; 0 where there are none. Every heading is always present.

escalates.description: How many products carry `escalate`: how many to see a professional about, without saying which.

locked.description: A verified user is given the full verdict.

fit.description: `not-ready` when the goal-fit check has not answered yet: the products it would decide are shown as kept for now, and it is tried again.

products.description: One per skin-care product on the shelf, in shelf order.

tapers.description: The step-downs the `stop` verdicts use, each once.

title.description: The heading, e.g. "Helping". `undecided` is shown as "Still checking".

intro.description: One or two plain sentences about the products under the heading.

count.description: How many products are under it; 0 where there are none.

entryId.description: The shelf entry this is about: its `id` from `GET /api/v1/me/shelf`.

kind.description: The shelf entry's own kind: `product` carries `product`; `no-label` carries `noLabel`. Absent only when the shelf entry can no longer be shown (it was taken off the shelf since the verdict was built): the product is still here, with its verdict, and carries neither.

allOf.description: Only on a `product` entry: the same summary `GET /api/v1/me/shelf` shows for it.

usedFor.description: How long the product has been used.

description.description: What the user noted, if anything.

concerns.description: Cautions for a product of unknown contents, worked out from the answers each time the item is shown. Not an analysis of any label.

rulesVersion.description: Which version of the caution rules wrote `concerns`.

noLabel.description: Only on a `no-label` entry: the same view `GET /api/v1/me/shelf` shows for it.

group.description: The heading the product is shown under.

reason.description: Why, in words for the user.

escalate.description: True when the user should see a professional about this product.

sameJobAs.description: Only on a `redundant` product: the entry id of the product that stays and does its job.

nudge.description: Only on a `cant-tell` product: what to do to get it read.

basis.description: Where the verdict comes from: every reason once, reviewed rules first. Empty for an `undecided` product, which the checker has not answered about yet. Copy awaiting the owner's sign-off.

suggest.description: One or more (usually one to three) fixed lines on what to do with the product, worked out from `verdict` alone (and `escalate`, and the `cant-tell` group). Copy awaiting the owner's sign-off.

maxFrequency.description: Keep it, but no more often than this.

taperCode.description: The `code` of the step-down in `tapers` to follow.

ShelfVerdictAction.description: What to do with the product: `keep` it, `reduce` it, `stop` it by a step-down, or `drop` it at once.

source.description: `ingredient-rule`: a reviewed rule about an ingredient the product holds. `claim-word`: a reviewed claim word the product's name makes.

statement.description: The rule's own words, or for a `claim-word` a fixed sentence naming the word. Shown as it is, and the same as `line`.

sourceUrl.description: A link to the source the rule rests on; null when it has none, and then the app shows no link.

reviewerRole.description: Who reviewed the rule, e.g. "a consultant dermatologist"; null for a rule stored before contract 2.4.0, and then the app shows no "Reviewed by" line.

line.description: The line to show, as it is.

ShelfVerdictBasis.description: One reason behind a verdict, for "Where this comes from". Saved with the product when the verdict is built, so a later edit to a rule does not change it.

code.description: The step-down's code, as a `stop` verdict names it.

fromWeek.description: The first week of the step, counting from 1.

toWeek.description: The last week of the step; the same as `fromWeek` for a single week.

schedule.description: The steps in order, ending with `stop`.

whoToSee.description: What kind of professional to see.

ShelfVerdictProfessional.description: "Talk to a professional" about a product: who to see, how soon and what to tell them, from the reviewed workbook. Null until the team has imported it. Never on the locked preview.

note.description: What looks wrong, in the person's own words. Trimmed; at most 500 characters once trimmed (more is 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`); empty or spaces only is no note. Only the team reads it.

Routine.description: `pending`: there is nothing to show yet (a first build is on its way, or the routine no longer fits the safety answers and is being rebuilt). `ready`: the routine in force. `updating`: the routine in force, while a newer one is being built.

startedOn.description: Day 1 of the routine, as `YYYY-MM-DD`: the day after the user tapped Start, in their local calendar once a time zone is stored (UTC otherwise); fixed when set, so a later change of time zone does not move it. Null until they tap Start. Step-down dates count from it.

expectation.description: What to expect and when, in plain words.

morning.description: The morning list, in routine order (cleanse, treat, moisturise, protect). The sunscreen is only ever here.

evening.description: The evening list, in routine order. Anything used less than daily (every other day, weekly, as needed) is here.

notInRoutine.description: The shelf products the routine was built without, in the shelf's order: stopped ones (`stepping-down`) and dropped ones (`left-out`). Products used less often stay in the lists. Fixed when the routine was built. Null for a routine built before the list was kept (unknown, not none); it gains one at its next rebuild.

label.description: The goal as the goal chips name it.

goal.description: The goal the routine was built for.

keepUsing.description: Shelf products used as they are. A sunscreen the rules would reduce counts here too: sun protection is never used less.

useLessOrChange.description: Shelf products to use less often, or to leave out (redundant, in the way of the goal, or not clear enough to keep).

products.description: The products being stopped step by step, as in `tapers`.

message.description: The fixed sentence for the card, naming the products.

stepDown.description: Null when nothing is being stopped.

RoutineSummary.description: Null for a routine built before summaries were kept; it gains one at its next rebuild.

title.description: The product in plain words ("Gel cleanser", "Niacinamide serum", "Sunscreen"): a capital, no full stop.

when.description: How often, in words for the card: "Every day", "Every other evening", "Once a week" or "When you need it".

reason.description: Why, in words for the user.

status.description: `active` for a step in the routine as written. `paused`: left out for now. `held`: left out while a hold is open. `bringing-back`: used again at a gentler pace.

changed.description: True when this step's product or frequency differs from the routine the user was last shown, or that routine had no such step. Always false the first time a routine is shown.

RoutineEntry.description: One card of the Morning or Evening list. A step used morning and evening is the same entry in both lists.

entryId.description: The shelf entry to keep using: its `id` from `GET /api/v1/me/shelf`.

brand.description: Null when the label was not read.

RoutineOwnProduct.description: A product already on the shelf.

code.description: The catalog code of the product.

origin.description: Only on a product a brand submitted for review, which says so. The review fee never affects the choice.

currency.description: The currency of the country the profile shops in.

price.description: The price range in the shopping country; null when it is not sold there.

whereSold.description: Where to find it in the shopping country; null when it is not sold there or the review does not say.

soldInCurrentCountry.description: False when the product is not sold in the shopping country (or has been retired): it stays on the screen, and `find-sold-here` asks for another.

soldElsewhere.description: The codes of the other countries that sell it; empty for a retired product.

notYetGot.description: True until the user taps "I got it".

RoutineRecommendedProduct.description: A product from the catalog the user does not have yet.

RoutineNoProduct.description: "Use what you have": nothing to recommend for this step.

entryId.description: The shelf entry: its `id` from `GET /api/v1/me/shelf`. It may have left the shelf since the routine was built.

title.description: The product in plain words, as the routine titles one.

status.description: `stepping-down`: being stopped step by step (see `tapers`). `left-out`: not part of the routine.

reason.description: The verdict's own one-line reason for the product, as it was when the routine was built.

entryId.description: The shelf entry being stepped down.

fromWeek.description: The first week of the step, counting from 1.

toWeek.description: The last week of the step; the same as `fromWeek` for a single week.

fromDate.description: The first day of the step, as `YYYY-MM-DD`: a calendar date, the person's local date once a time zone is stored (UTC otherwise), fixed when the step-down began. Only once the routine is started.

toDate.description: The last day of the step, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, counted from `fromDate` in calendar days. Only once the routine is started.

steps.description: The steps in order, ending with `stop`.

startedOn.description: Day 1 of the routine, as `YYYY-MM-DD`: the day after the user tapped Start, in their local calendar once a time zone is stored (UTC otherwise); fixed when set, so a later change of time zone does not move it. Null until they tap Start. Step-down dates count from it.

expectation.description: What to expect and when, in plain words.

morning.description: The morning list, in routine order (cleanse, treat, moisturise, protect). The sunscreen is only ever here.

evening.description: The evening list, in routine order. Anything used less than daily (every other day, weekly, as needed) is here.

notInRoutine.description: The shelf products the routine was built without, in the shelf's order: stopped ones (`stepping-down`) and dropped ones (`left-out`). category.description: The step's plain noun: Cleanser, Treatment, Moisturiser or Sunscreen.

lookFor.description: What to look for in this kind of product. For a person who is pregnant or breastfeeding it is the guide's pregnancy-safe text when it has one.

guide.description: Reviewed copy for the step, written for the person's goal when the guide has a row for it.

typicalPrice.description: The lowest price to the highest price across every reviewed product for the step in the shopping country, not only the ones listed; null when there are none.

commonlySoldAt.description: Up to three places that most of those products are sold at, most common first.

products.description: At most ten reviewed products that suit the person: the routine's pick first, then the cheapest.

code.description: The catalog code of the product.

origin.description: Only on a product a brand submitted for review, which says so. The review fee never affects the choice.

aboutPrice.description: About what it costs: the lowest price it is sold at in the country the profile shops in.

whereSold.description: Where to find it in the shopping country; null when the review does not say.

why.description: One fixed line on why this product is here: the concerns of the goal it works on, in plain words.

inYourRoutine.description: True for the product the routine recommends for this step; it is listed first.

started.description: Whether the routine in force has a day 1 (Start was tapped). False with no routine, with one a safety change hides, and with one not started.

day.description: The person's local day, `YYYY-MM-DD`: their stored time zone's, else UTC (also for a stored zone that cannot be used).

startsOn.description: Day 1, `YYYY-MM-DD`, once started. Start makes tomorrow day 1, so on the day of the tap it is ahead of `day`.

week.description: The week of the plan, counted from day 1 with no cap. Null before day 1 and when not started.

card.description: The reviewed card for the week, written for the current goal and for a step-down when the team has written one. Null before day 1, and when no card is approved for the week.

half.description: The current half of the local day: morning before 15:00, evening from 15:00. Fixed; not the reminder times.

done.description: Whether the person ticked this half off today (`POST /api/v1/me/routine/check-ins`).

entries.description: What is due in this half today, in routine order. A paused or held step, an as-needed step and a step on its rest day are left out.

done.description: Whether the person ticked this half off today (`POST /api/v1/me/routine/check-ins`).

entries.description: What is due in this half today, in routine order. A paused or held step, an as-needed step and a step on its rest day are left out.

other.description: The other half of the day.

stepDowns.description: Each step-down that is running, with where it is.

step.description: Null for the check-in that has no step (nothing could be paused).

title.description: The routine's title for the step; null with no step.

checkInsDue.description: The check-ins after a pause that are due, until answered.

hold.description: Set while a hold is open.

bringingBack.description: Each step being brought back after a pause, on rest days too.

title.description: The routine's title for the step.

checkDay.description: The day the person is asked how the skin is, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

paused.description: Each step that is paused (or being held for a professional) and so left out of the halves, with the day it is checked.

remindersOff.description: True when reminders are not switched on: show the banner.

link.description: An in-app path to open when the item is tapped.

latest.description: The newest five items, newest first, read or not.

title.description: The product in plain words ("Gel cleanser", "Niacinamide serum", "Sunscreen"): a capital, no full stop.

when.description: How often, in words for the card: "Every day", "Every other evening", "Once a week" or "When you need it".

reason.description: Why, in words for the user.

status.description: `active`, or `bringing-back` for a step used again at a gentler pace after a pause. A paused or held step is not listed.

TodayEntry.description: One card of a half of the day: the routine's entry, without `changed`.

day.description: The local day checked in for, `YYYY-MM-DD`: today or yesterday in the person's time zone (UTC with none stored), and not before day 1.

timeZone.description: The IANA time zone, or null until the phone reports one.

missedDaysChannel.description: Where the missed-days nudge goes. Read-only: `whatsapp` only when WhatsApp is an enabled channel here and the account has a verified phone, otherwise `push`.

enabled.description: Remind me at the times below.

morning.description: When to be reminded in the morning as a 24-hour time, `HH:MM`. Anything else is 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

evening.description: When to be reminded in the evening as a 24-hour time, `HH:MM`. Anything else is 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

timeZone.description: The phone's IANA time zone. Anything Intl does not know, and a fixed offset such as `+01:00`, is 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. The canonical name is stored (`africa/lagos` becomes `Africa/Lagos`). `null` clears it, and local days fall back to UTC.

stepDownAlerts.description: Tell me when a step-down changes what I do.

missedDaysNudge.description: Nudge me when I have missed some days.

kind.description: What happened, such as `reminder`, `step-down` or `rest-night`. Open-ended: show the title and body, not a name picked from the kind.

day.description: The local calendar day the item is about, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

link.description: An in-app path to open when the item is tapped.

items.description: Newest first. Items are kept for good.

next.description: Send as `before` for the next, older page. Null when no older item follows.

unread.description: How many items are still unread.

upTo.description: The id of an item. It and every older item are marked read.

day.description: The local calendar day of the log, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

items.description: What the person is noticing: `stinging-or-burning`, `new-redness`, `tightness-or-dryness`, `new-breakouts`, `itching`, `swelling`, `pus-or-hot-patch` or `nothing-unusual`. `nothing-unusual` only ever stands alone.

howBad.description: How bad it is, one choice: `mild`, `noticeable` or `hard-to-ignore`.

outcome.description: What the log came to, as it was decided (a `pause` the rules came to may end as `professional` or `nothing-to-pause`).

howBad.description: How bad it is, one choice: `mild`, `noticeable` or `hard-to-ignore`.

facts.description: What the person logged, repeated back on the professional screen.

response.description: The reviewed text, with `{step}` already filled: a list for `advice` (one for each thing noticed), one text for `pause`, `nothing-to-pause` and `expected-flare`, the professional text for `professional`, and null for `logged`.

title.description: The routine's own title for the paused step.

checkDay.description: The local day the person is asked how it feels, `YYYY-MM-DD`: three days on.

paused.description: The pause this log made; null for every outcome but `pause`.

items.description: What the person is noticing: `stinging-or-burning`, `new-redness`, `tightness-or-dryness`, `new-breakouts`, `itching`, `swelling`, `pus-or-hot-patch` or `nothing-unusual`. `nothing-unusual` only ever stands alone.

noticing.description: At least one. A symptom named twice counts once.

note.description: Optional, at most 500 characters (counted as characters, not bytes). It is stored and shown back only on the professional screen; no rule reads it.

day.description: The local calendar day of the log, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

items.description: What the person is noticing: `stinging-or-burning`, `new-redness`, `tightness-or-dryness`, `new-breakouts`, `itching`, `swelling`, `pus-or-hot-patch` or `nothing-unusual`. `nothing-unusual` only ever stands alone.

howBad.description: How bad it is, one choice: `mild`, `noticeable` or `hard-to-ignore`.

outcome.description: What the log came to, as it was decided (a `pause` the rules came to may end as `professional` or `nothing-to-pause`).

logs.description: The last 20, newest first. Never the note.

state.description: `undone` for a first pause. `bringing-back` for a pause made again while the step was being brought back: the step goes back on its ladder, never straight to full strength.

outcome.description: What the answer came to. Branch on `kind`.

response.description: The reviewed text, with `{step}` already filled, for `calmer` and `same`; the reviewed professional text (`whoToSee`, `howSoon`, `whatToTellThem`) for `professional`.

step.description: Null for the check-in with no step.

state.description: `bringing-back` after calmer on a step, `ended` after calmer on the check-in with no step, `paused` after same, `escalated` after a professional result.

checkDay.description: The next local day to ask, `YYYY-MM-DD`; null unless the pause is still `paused`.

id.description: The pause's id, for the check-in route.

step.description: Null for the check-in with no step.

checkDay.description: The local day it is due, `YYYY-MM-DD`: today or earlier.

checkInsDue.description: The check-ins due on the day of the close: the steps the hold kept out, each due today, and any other check-in already due.

how.description: How the hold ends: `seen` (the person saw a professional) or `settled` (the skin has settled).

version.description: The version of the face photo consent wording the user agreed to. Only the current version is accepted.

current.description: True while the consent is for the current wording and has not been withdrawn: the only consent a face scan accepts.

version.description: The version of the face share consent wording the user agreed to. Only the current version is accepted.

current.description: True while the consent is for the current wording and has not been withdrawn: the only consent a share accepts.

afterScanId.description: The face scan to show as "after": a later ready scan of the current goal, with a front photo, at least 14 days after day one.

imageUrl.description: The product's stock image, an absolute URL, if it has one.

products.description: At most 10, best first: those whose search text (brand, name and variant, normalised) starts with the query, then the others, each group by that text.

locale.description: The language the text is in: `en`, whatever was asked for.

contentVersion.description: A hash of everything below. It is also the `ETag` (in quotes).

placeholder.description: Placeholder of the box where the user types a goal in their own words.

chips.description: The goals to offer, in display order. Each `id` is accepted by `PUT /api/v1/me/goal`.

answers.description: The answer card for each goal. It is the same text `PUT /api/v1/me/goal` answers with, without `note`.

colourNote.description: Add to the answer card only when the user's own words asked to be lighter. It is the `note` that `PUT /api/v1/me/goal` sends in that case.

get.summary: What to do with each product on the shelf
get.description: Guests included, but a guest is never given the full verdict. For every skin-care product on the profile's shelf, a verified user is told: keep it, reduce it, stop it by a step-down, or drop it, with the reason in words for the user. The verdict is built in the background, never in this request. `{ status: 'pending' }` means a build is on its way (this ask queues it when none is fresh): ask again shortly. A verdict built before the shelf, the safety answers, the goal, the face scan or the rules changed is never served as if it were current; the answer is `pending` until the new one is built. `status: 'ready'` carries `locked` and `fit` (`not-ready` when the goal-fit check failed: those products are counted as `undecided` and kept for now, and it is tried again). A verified user's ready verdict has `locked: false`, `products` and `tapers`: the step-downs that the `stop` verdicts name by `taperCode`, each once. A guest's has `locked: true` and a preview only: `total` (how many products), `counts` (how many under each heading, 0 where none) and `escalates` (how many to see a professional about), and no product, reason or step-down; it is the same saved verdict, so signing up shows the full one at once with no new build. 503 `VERDICT_UNAVAILABLE` while the steroid or the lightening-agent step-down is not approved yet (checked first, even for a profile with no goal). 409 `GOAL_REQUIRED` for a profile with no goal.

get.summary: Follow the shelf verdict live, as server-sent events
get.description: Guests included, who are only ever sent the locked preview. A `text/event-stream`, not the usual envelope (errors before the stream starts still are). The gates and the build are those of `GET /api/v1/me/verdict`: 503 `VERDICT_UNAVAILABLE` while the steroid or the lightening-agent step-down is not approved yet (checked first), then 409 `GOAL_REQUIRED` for a profile with no goal; otherwise this ask queues the build when none is fresh. Frames: `snapshot` first, whose data is the body `GET /api/v1/me/verdict` answers now for the caller (`{ status: 'pending' }`, the full verdict for a verified user or the locked preview for a guest); then one `verdict` each time a build saves, whose data is the ready verdict in that same shape (a guest never receives a product on it); then `done` (data `{}`) after a `verdict` whose `fit` is `ready`, or whose goal-fit check has had its retry (nothing more is coming soon), after which the server closes the stream. A verdict whose `fit` is `not-ready` while a try is still to come is not followed by `done`: the check is tried again and its `verdict` arrives on the open stream. A `verdict` of `{ status: 'pending' }` (no `done`) means the shelf or answers changed while the verdict was being built: the new one is on its way on the same stream. A verdict that is already current and finished gets `snapshot` and `done` at once. A `: ping` comment arrives every 20 seconds while nothing else does. The server closes a stream 10 minutes after it opened; reconnect to carry on, the new `snapshot` is the current state. Send the bearer token as for every other route, which a browser `EventSource` cannot: use `fetch` and read the body.

get.description: A `text/event-stream`, not the usual envelope (errors before the stream starts still are). Frames: `snapshot` first, whose data is the scan exactly as `GET /api/v1/scans/products/{scanId}` returns it; then, on a shelf scan, one `photo` for each photo as it is read (state and `skipped` counts, as that response shows them), always before the `item` events of its products; then one `item` per change, whose data is the item as that response shows it; then `done` (data `{}`) once every item is `ready`, `rejected`, `failed` or `unidentified`, after which the server closes the stream. The server closes a stream 10 minutes after it opened; reconnect to carry on, the new `snapshot` is the current state. Send the bearer token as for every other route, which a browser `EventSource` cannot: use `fetch` and read the body. Another user's scan is 404, the same as one that does not exist.

post.summary: Start a face scan from a front photo and optionally two side photos
post.description: A guest may call this. Multipart: a `front` part, and optionally `right` and `left`. Every photo must be a JPEG of at most 6,000,000 bytes, with a shorter side of at least 1080 and a longer side of at most 4096 pixels. The checks run in this order and nothing is stored until all pass: 409 `FACE_CONSENT_REQUIRED` (no current consent for this profile), 409 `GOAL_REQUIRED` (pick a goal first), 429 `FACE_SCAN_NOT_DUE`: the current goal's chase gets one scan, plus one wider check-in scan at its review point (issue #145). `details.reason` is `already-scanned-for-goal` (the chase already has a scan, or its check-in is still being analysed or needs a retake), `check-in-not-due` (the chase has its day one but has not reached its review point yet; `details.checkInDueAt` says when it will) or `check-in-taken` (the chase's check-in has already been taken) or `scan-limit` (a new chase's first scan waits 30 days after the profile's last day-one scan under any goal; check-ins neither count nor are limited; `details.nextScanAt` says when), then the photos: 400 `UNSUPPORTED_IMAGE`, `IMAGE_TOO_SMALL` or `IMAGE_TOO_LARGE`, and 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` without a `front`. One bad photo refuses the whole scan. The answer is 202 with the scan `analysing`; if the analysis cannot be queued the scan is `failed` with reason `unavailable` (still 202), and a new scan may be started. Starting a scan costs nothing in the AI spend ledger. The answer shows no result; a guest follows the scan with `GET /api/v1/scans/faces/{id}/events` and must verify to read it. A per-address and a per-user limit apply: 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`.

post.description: A guest may call this. Multipart with a `front` part only, a JPEG held to the same rules as when the scan was started. For a scan whose `state` is `needs-retake`. post.summary: Perfect Corp tells us an analysis task has ended
post.description: Called by Perfect Corp, not by the app. Public: the Standard Webhooks signature (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature`) on the raw body is the credential, and a delivery that is not correctly signed, is older than 5 minutes, or is not the webhook's shape is 401 `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID`. A signed delivery is 200 `{ received: true }` whether or not it matches a scan of this environment (a task from another environment, or of a deleted scan, is ignored). A delivery that matches is queued for the analysis job, which asks Perfect Corp for the result itself; a delivery that cannot be queued is 503 `WEBHOOK_UNAVAILABLE`, so Perfect Corp sends it again, and the same `webhook-id` delivered twice runs the job once. Register this address for each environment in the Perfect Corp console.

post.summary: Check, and optionally apply, an edited catalog workbook
post.description: Multipart. The whole workbook is the upload: a product, rule or country code it leaves out is retired, never deleted. The server checks the workbook against the contract itself, refuses one made for another contract version (409 `CONTRACT_MISMATCH`, checked before anything else), refuses one made from a catalog version that is not live (409 `CATALOG_STALE`), and reports the diff per tab. The default is a dry run that writes nothing. With `dryRun=false` and the original `.xlsx` as `file`, the file is archived and the change applied in one atomic write, which the catalog version guards. Problems with the workbook come as 400 `CATALOG_INVALID` with `error.details.problems`: `{ tab, row, column, rule }`, never a cell value. In production, an approved Tapers, Guides, Reintroductions, Escalations, Responses or Weeks row whose `approved_by` is not on the server's list of qualified approvers is such a problem too (`UNQUALIFIED_APPROVER`). A workbook of the current contract version that is not eleven tabs of a header row and rows is 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`, checked after the contract version. Other 400 codes: `CATALOG_FILE_REQUIRED` (applying without a file), `CATALOG_FILE_TOO_LARGE` (over 10 MB), `CATALOG_FILE_NOT_XLSX` (not a zip, so not an .xlsx) and `CATALOG_TOO_LARGE` (the change is too many rows for one atomic write; it is never split, so make it in smaller uploads). 503 `CATALOG_ARCHIVE_FAILED` means the file could not be archived and nothing was applied; try again.

workbook.description: The JSON text of the workbook (the `workbook` of an export, edited): an object of the eleven tabs described by `CatalogWorkbook`. Only that it is a JSON object is checked first; the tabs are checked after `contractVersion`.

file.description: The .xlsx the workbook was read from, up to 10 MB. Archived when the upload is applied; required when `dryRun` is `false`.

baseVersion.description: The `catalogVersion` of the export the workbook was edited from.

dryRun.description: Only `false` applies the upload. The default reports what it would change and writes nothing.

contractVersion.description: The `contractVersion` of the export the workbook was edited from. A workbook made for another contract version is refused with 409 `CONTRACT_MISMATCH`, before anything else is checked.

uploadedBy.description: Who is uploading, as a label for the catalog version (1 to 80 characters, after trimming).
